original_title: Trastuzumab Deruxtecan in Metastatic Urothelial Carcinoma with NGS-Detected ERBB2 Amplification: A Four-Patient Real-World Case Series
title: Four patients, an NGS-only HER2 call, and T-DXd
blurb: A real-world case series of four metastatic urothelial carcinoma patients put on trastuzumab deruxtecan based solely on NGS-detected ERBB2 amplification, since IHC and ISH confirmation weren't available. N=4 is barely a series, but it's a data point on whether sequencing alone is enough to pick T-DXd patients.

original_title: Efficacy and safety of trastuzumab emtansine versus trastuzumab deruxtecan in HER2-positive breast cancer with anti-HER2 therapy resistance: a multicenter retrospective study
title: T-DM1 vs T-DXd after anti-HER2 resistance, a five-center retrospective
blurb: A multicenter Chinese retrospective pitting T-DM1 against T-DXd in HER2-positive breast cancer that's already stopped responding to anti-HER2 therapy, comparing efficacy and safety and picking out what predicts progression-free survival. Retrospective, not randomized, so it's hypothesis-generating rather than a verdict on which ADC to reach for next.

original_title: Formaldehyde hydroformylation over a heterogeneous catalyst based on a functionalized rhodium-biphosphine unit
title: Turning formaldehyde into something useful with a rhodium-biphosphine catalyst
blurb: A heterogeneous catalyst built around a functionalized rhodium-biphosphine unit, applied to formaldehyde hydroformylation. Title's all there is to go on here, no yields given, so it's one to watch for the actual numbers.

original_title: Anderson‐Type Polyoxometalates Intercalated Cobalt–Copper Layered Double Hydroxides Heterostructures With Plum Blossom‐Like for Efficient Electroreduction of Nitrate to Ammonia
title: Plum-blossom-shaped Co-Cu hydroxides for turning nitrate into ammonia
blurb: A {ZnMo6} Anderson-type polyoxometalate anchored onto copper-cobalt layered double hydroxide, grown into a plum-blossom heterostructure, for electrochemically reducing nitrate to ammonia. The pitch is synergy between the POM cluster and the LDH support, which is exactly what every heterogeneous nitrate-reduction paper claims, so it's worth checking whether the activity numbers actually back it up.

original_title: Citrate-mediated structure and enthalpy-entropy trade-off in Ni-CeO2 catalysts for low-temperature CO2 methanation
title: CO2 methanation catalysts live or die on entropy, not just enthalpy
blurb: Ni-CeO2 catalysts for low-temperature CO2 methanation, with citrate as the structure-directing ingredient, get judged by the enthalpy-entropy trade-off that actually sets the activation free energy, rather than the enthalpy number the field usually quotes on its own. A useful corrective if activity trends have been read off the wrong term.

original_title: Multifunctional Injectable Hydrogel as a Biomimic Lens: Optical-Mechanical Restoration and Dynamic Postoperative Microenvironment Regulation.
title: An injectable hydrogel meant to double as an artificial lens
blurb: A multifunctional injectable hydrogel pitched as a biomimetic lens replacement, restoring both optical and mechanical function while managing the eye's postoperative microenvironment as it heals. Light on detail beyond the concept, but swapping a rigid lens implant for something injectable is the interesting part.

original_title: Efficacy and safety of trastuzumab deruxtecan in patients with HER2-expressing biliary tract or pancreatic tumors: a subgroup analysis of DESTINY-PanTumor02
title: T-DXd's benefit, narrowed to bile duct and pancreatic tumors
blurb: DESTINY-PanTumor02 already showed T-DXd working across HER2-expressing tumors regardless of where they started. This is the subgroup cut for biliary tract and pancreatic cancer specifically, patients with HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+ tumors who'd already run out of other treatment lines. Pancreatic cancer responding to much of anything is rare enough that this cohort is the one to watch.

original_title: Cellular responses to targeted radionuclide therapy: rethinking radiobiology under continuous low dose rates.
title: Radiobiology built for one big dose, meeting a therapy that trickles
blurb: Targeted radionuclide therapy delivers its dose continuously and at low rate, not the single acute burst most radiobiology models were built around. The argument here is that the cellular response playbook needs rewriting to match, not borrowed wholesale from external beam radiotherapy.

original_title: Atomic-precision π-driven peptide hydrogel nanofibers with ordered water channels.
title: A peptide hydrogel that knows where its water goes
blurb: Nanofibers self-assembled from peptides via pi-stacking to atomic precision, with ordered water channels running through the structure instead of the usual disordered hydrogel soak. Getting that level of structural control over water in a soft material is the actual feat here.

original_title: An Overview of Mass Spectrometry-Based Methods to Analyze Post-Translational Modifications.
title: A rundown of how mass spec catches post-translational modifications
blurb: A methods chapter walking through the mass-spec approaches used to detect PTMs, phosphorylation, glycosylation, and the usual suspects. A protocols reference to keep on the shelf, not a new result.

original_title: Quantitative Renal Scintigraphy for Differentiating Ischemic and Nonischemic Transplant Complications: A Biopsy-Controlled Study.
title: Telling a rejecting kidney transplant from a starved one, by scintigraphy
blurb: Quantitative renal scintigraphy tested against biopsy to sort whether a transplant complication is ischemic or something else entirely. Biopsy-controlled means they actually checked the imaging call against ground truth, which is more rigor than most imaging studies bother with.

original_title: Why does pressurized chlorine flow slowly?
title: Why does pressurized chlorine flow slowly?
blurb: Hello! I have two glass ampoules, one of bromine and the other of pressurized chlorine. For some reason, the chlorine flows much slower than my bromine. It takes over two seconds for the liquid chlorine air bubble to travel from one side to the other. Google AI is saying that bromine has a higher viscosity, so it should be thicker and flow slower, but my experience is the complete opposite. Could any of you explain in detail why this is the case? My chlorine shouldn't be fake because I bought it from the highly reputable Metallium (ElementSales) website. I also spent nearly $200 on it.
